 By Nick Wire Nov 17, 2026 • 11:00 am
 Share via facebook Share via X Share via email The Los Angeles Lakers ramp up their schedule again tonight after a miniature break of two games in six days. The Lakers play four home games in the next six days, starting with a matchup tonight against the Charlotte Hornets. 
 Both teams enter tonight's matchup with a bit of a limp - as Lakers' starting center Walker Kessler and starting shooting guard Austin Reaves will miss tonight's game while Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schröder are inactive for the Hornets tonight. 
 The Lakers will still have the best player on the court, Luka Dončić, who's averaging 39 points, 7.8 assists and 7.2 rebounds while shooting 48.6% from the field. Dončić has been on a tear - one that that we haven't seen since prime James Harden averaged nearly 36-8-7 in 2019. 
 After trading away LaMelo Ball in the offseason, the Hornets have relied heavily on their forward core - including Naz Reid who they acquired in the package for Ball. Reid is averaging 17.2 points and 8.2 rebounds so far this season. 
 The Hornets' other forward, Brandon Miller, is averaging 19.2 and 4.7 this season. Miller was taken second overall in the 2023 NBA Draft, and though he can be inefficient, he is a high-volume scorer that can pour in 30+ on any given night.

 First Pick: Jake LaRavia over 4.5 rebounds 
 Rundown:  With Kessler out, starting power forward Jake LaRavia will have increased rebounding duties. He's stepped into this role nicely before. Against the Clippers on Oct. 28, LaRavia had 10 rebounds and two blocks while Kessler was tied up with Brook Lopez and the Clippers' athletic forwards. LaRavia is already good for at-least three rebounds per game - now with Kessler and Reaves out - that's ~ 14 rebounds that'll need to be accounted for.
 Second Pick: Luka Dončić over 36.5 points 
 Rundown: This is a don't overthink it pick. Dončić is down his two best teammates. This is a game against a worse opponent that the Lakers should comfortably win when fully healthy - but because they're shorthanded, the Lakers will need Dončić to score a lot. The Lakers also don't really have any great scorers besides Dončić and Reaves - however Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes are capable of putting up 20-25 on any given night when their name is called.  
 The Hornets have a very decent defensive rating of 106.7 this season - however against point guards that rating skyrockets to 117.4. Dončić should produce well against this matchup.
